source_links_enforced_means: The flag asserts that every MEASURED cell records all five mandated source layers with a date on each check; that a layer recorded as found carries what it yielded and a link resolving to that row's own trial identifier; and that a layer recorded as not available carries a reason and a date. title: Intravenous iron against placebo or usual care in heart failure with iron deficiency: six outcomes under four effect measures, pooled within three families and across none, with the two endpoints that carry no ordinary interval reported from single trials
question: In adults with heart failure and iron deficiency, what is the effect of intravenous iron compared with placebo or usual care on recurrent hospitalisations for heart failure with and without cardiovascular death, on the time to a first such event, on death from any cause, on a hierarchical composite of death, hospitalisation and walk distance, and on exercise capacity itself -- with each of those questions answered separately?
_prose_rule: Every text field is PROSE unless it is on the validator's numeric list. Prose may not restate a number the object holds structurally.
_sourcing_rule: Every measured input carries the verbatim sentence it was read from, EXTRACTED from a staged payload by anchor rather than typed, and a resolvable link to the layer it was read from. Every cell records all five mandated source layers with a date, so a layer that held nothing is distinguishable from a layer nobody opened. Derived transforms are computed here and are not claimed to appear in any source.
_estimand_rule: FOUR EFFECT MEASURES, SIX OUTCOMES, THREE POOLED FAMILIES, AND NO CONVERSION ANYWHERE. TWO of the four measures print ratios below one here, a third prints a ratio ABOVE one on which above-one is the FAVOURABLE direction, and the fourth prints metres against a null of zero. An earlier version of this rule said three of the four print numbers below one, which is false of the win ratio and is exactly the reading this object exists to prevent -- a reader who scans for numbers below one and finds the pattern confirmed will carry it onto the one row where it inverts. Nothing here is converted into anything else and no pool crosses an estimand. The hardest case in this review is not a measure at all -- it is one trial whose second primary endpoint counts hospitalisations with no death component while two other trials' primaries count the same hospitalisations WITH cardiovascular death, and all three are rate ratios below one. No effect-measure check in this repository could have separated them, which is why the separation is structural.
single_tier_because: The primary tier is NOT uniform in this object. Nine of the ten measured cells are sourced to a primary publication and ONE is sourced to a registry results record, because that trial's publication does not report that outcome at all. A cell's tier follows where its value actually came from, and on the one row where two layers both hold the cell and DISAGREE, the tier names the layer the stored value came from and the other layer's value is stored beside it as a divergence.
completeness_statement: FULL BUILD, with a stated boundary on the search and with a REDISCOVERY TEST behind it rather than an assertion that a search ran. Every randomised trial the staged search record ENUMERATES -- the trials this review contains, the trials the two prior syntheses name in their own lists, and the ongoing trials at or above the enrolment threshold that record applies -- is either contributing here, or in ONE screening log with the eligibility criterion it fails and the quantity it reports instead, or listed as eligible and not yet reporting. What is NOT claimed, and what an earlier version of this sentence did claim, is a disposition for every hit the class-keyed query returns: that query returns far more records than this object classifies, and the staged record scopes its own enumeration by size rather than silently. A reader who wants the unenumerated tail should read the query in that record and run it. There is exactly ONE source list, `screening.records`; `screening.excluded` is a view COMPUTED from it at build time, row for row, so it cannot say anything the records do not. What this statement does NOT claim is a systematic multi-database search: none was run, the limitation is recorded in the screening block, and SOME of the screened-out records are characterised from a prior synthesis's table rather than from the trials' own reports. How many is deliberately NOT asserted in this sentence: it is COMPUTED from the records at build time into the screening block, and each of those rows says on itself that it rests on that table. An earlier version typed a count here that was wrong by one against the object's own array, which is what a prose copy of a countable fact does.

verification_basis.what_verifies_this_object: Two things, and neither is a badge this repository can emit about itself. The object is the single source of truth and the page is a pure projection of it, so a claim on the page that is not in the object cannot exist. And the object is read by two model families with independent file access, from different vendors, each asked to find a defect in the ACTUAL object rather than to approve it.
verification_basis.what_is_not_claimed: No internal check is described as independent verification. A script that reads this object and reports it consistent has confirmed consistency and nothing else. What CAN be said about the arithmetic here is narrower and is worth saying precisely: every pooled figure was computed twice, by this builder and by a separate script, and checked against an external meta-analysis engine, and the two internal paths share no code beyond the estimator module they both call.
verification_basis.bar: Both families must find no defect in the object. A finding about the validator is not a finding about the object and does not block.

handbook.conformance: Sections 3.2.1, 3.2.2 and 3.2.3 fix the axes on which ELIGIBILITY turns -- population, intervention and comparator -- and every screening decision names which of them it falls on, which is why the screening log has a criterion column rather than a verdict column. Section 3.2.4 is cited for the caution it gives AGAINST making eligibility depend on which outcomes a study reported, AND because this review must be honest that it applies an outcome criterion at eligibility anyway: most of its screened-out records fail on that axis. The distinction the review rests on, and which a reader is entitled to reject, is between what a trial REPORTED and what it DESIGNATED. The caution is about letting selective reporting decide membership; the criterion here turns on the endpoint each trial REGISTERED as its primary before any result existed. That is checkable for the screened trials whose registry records are staged -- one registered a self-reported global assessment and functional class, the other a change in peak oxygen consumption -- and it is NOT checkable for those characterised from a prior synthesis's table, whose rows say so on themselves. The object carries six outcomes rather than admitting only the trials that report one of them, and no trial is screened out for reporting a quantity in the wrong FORM. What this review DOES do, and an earlier version of this passage denied it, is exclude a trial that designates an endpoint this review holds but publishes no extractable estimate of it: the screened trial with a registered walk-distance secondary is out on the clinical-event criterion while the review carries a walk-distance estimand. That is a stricter rule than 3.2.4 requires, it is the review's own, and it is declared here rather than dressed as the Handbook's. Its cost is visible on the row, which quotes what that trial reports. Section 10.3 gives the METHOD by which every pool in this object is computed: log ratios combined by generic inverse variance. effect_measure: Both contributing trials report this endpoint as a rate ratio over recurrent events and no conversion is performed.
outcome_definition: Both count hospitalisations for heart failure and cardiovascular death, first and subsequent, and both say so in their own words on their own rows.
comparator: THIS IS THE LARGEST THING THIS POOL CROSSES AND IT IS EASY TO MISS. One trial randomised against a matching saline placebo. The other randomised against USUAL CARE, with no placebo infusion at all. A review whose eligibility demanded placebo would have excluded the second trial outright. The staged search record notes that the corrected query deliberately carries NO comparator requirement for exactly this reason. An earlier version of this row called that one of two defects the record exists to document, which over-reads it: the record exists to document a DRUG-NAME-keyed query failing to rediscover a contributing trial, and the comparator point is a note it carries alongside. The eligibility criterion is written to admit both comparator types.

The other is OPEN LABEL with masked adjudication of the outcomes -- a blinded-endpoint design, not a blinded-treatment one, and its registry record classifies it as masked to the outcome assessor only. hfh_cvd_recurrent.heterogeneity_status: Computed from Q and its single degree of freedom. With TWO trials this statistic has almost no power to detect heterogeneity, so a low value is consistent both with agreement and with not being able to tell, and it is reported with that caveat rather than as reassurance. What the statistic cannot see at all are the dimensions the uniformity table records, because those are differences in the question each trial answered rather than in its answer.

sensitivity.method: leave-one-out, plus a comparison of between-study variance estimators and of interval methods
sensitivity.authority: Cochrane Handbook version 6.5.1, section 10.14 for sensitivity analyses generally. Section 10.10.4.4 governs the estimator half: it records that methods other than DerSimonian and Laird estimate the between-study variance better and that restricted maximum likelihood is the current default. Section 10.10.4.5 is cited for the INTERVAL comparison and not for the estimator comparison; it concerns interpretation with few studies and the method it compares is the confidence interval.
sensitivity.decision_under_test: Whether the pooled estimate depends on either single trial, and whether it depends on the choice of between-study variance estimator and interval method.
sensitivity.leave_one_out_finding: With two trials a leave-one-out fit IS the other trial, and this table says so rather than presenting single-trial rows as though they were pooled sensitivity results. Read it as what it is: the two contributing trials' own estimates side by side, each with the interval it carries alone.

between_study_variance_method_comparison.why: Section 10.10.4.4 records restricted maximum likelihood as the current default and that estimators other than DerSimonian and Laird perform better; that is the whole of the authority for running this comparison. Nothing in the Handbook instructs a review to run it at a particular number of studies, and running it here is a choice made under section 10.14 because with two trials the choice is plausibly influential.
between_study_variance_method_comparison.estimator_kept: Restricted maximum likelihood with the ordinary interval, because section 10.10.4.4 records it as the current default and as a better estimator than DerSimonian and Laird. The Hartung-Knapp-Sidik-Jonkman interval is reported beside it with the floor on its scale factor applied, so it can widen the ordinary interval and can never come out narrower than it. It is NOT presented as the interval to prefer: section 10.10.4.5 says the opposite is possible, that with only two or three studies such intervals can be EXCESSIVELY WIDE and an ordinary interval may be preferable, and it asks for the comparison rather than for a winner.
between_study_variance_method_comparison.verdict: The three variance estimators agree, because with the between-study variance estimated at zero there is nothing for them to disagree about; at two studies that agreement is close to uninformative and is reported as arithmetic rather than as corroboration. The two INTERVAL METHODS are the informative half. On this estimand they DISAGREE about whether the null is excluded: the ordinary interval excludes it and the more conservative one does not. Neither is presented as deciding the question. What the disagreement establishes is how little two trials constrain a random-effects average, and it is carried into the imprecision domain, which is downgraded.

grade.starting_point_because: every contributing study is a randomised controlled trial

risk_of_bias.basis_in_sources: Both contributing trials are randomised and prospectively registered, and this endpoint is the PRIMARY of both, so none of the selective-reporting exposure a secondary endpoint carries applies to this estimand. What carries the SERIOUS rating is a single fact about one of them: it is OPEN LABEL, with no placebo infusion, so participants and treating clinicians knew the assignment. Its outcome adjudication is masked and its endpoint is adjudicated, which limits that exposure -- a hospitalisation is a harder endpoint than a symptom score -- but the DECISION to admit a patient is made by an unmasked clinician before any adjudicator sees it, and that is the step masking cannot protect. The other trial is double-blind and this domain is not about it. Rating a pool on its weaker member is the conservative reading and it is stated here rather than averaged away.

inconsistency.derived_from: Q against its single degree of freedom and the between-study variance, both stored in this result's heterogeneity block. With TWO trials this statistic has almost no power, so a rating of not serious means no heterogeneity was DETECTED and must not be read as evidence that the trials agree. Section 14.2.2 makes the trigger UNEXPLAINED heterogeneity rather than a value of the statistic, and it cross-references chapter ten for the bands; the dimensions on which these two trials genuinely differ are listed in the uniformity table rather than produced afterwards as explanations. Not downgraded, with that caveat stated rather than implied.

indirectness.basis_in_sources: Not downgraded, and the reasoning is worth stating because two candidates exist. The first is the population spread between an at-discharge and an ambulatory trial, which is diversity WITHIN the question this review asks rather than a mismatch between the question and the evidence, and it belongs to the uniformity table. The second is the crossing of two different iron preparations, which makes the pooled value a CLASS average; that is what the question asks for and it is labelled as such on the result and in the scope block. Downgrading for a reader's likely misreading would be stricter than the Handbook while claiming its support, which a gate leg has caught in this batch before.

imprecision.derived_from: The pooled interval stored in this result and the alternative-method interval reported beside it in the sensitivity block. Neither is turned into a threshold rule here: what carries the downgrade is recorded in the triggers below, and these two intervals are the arithmetic a reader can check it against.
imprecision.triggers_computed: Condition one, the ordinary interval excluding the null: reported against the stored pooled interval, where a reader can check it. Condition three, the optimal information size: NOT computable from what this object holds, and declared so below rather than treated as met. What carries the downgrade is the INTERVAL. On THIS estimand the ordinary interval excludes the null and the more conservative interval -- with the floor on its scale factor applied, so it can only widen the ordinary one and never narrow it -- does NOT. An interval consistent with no effect as well as with the benefit the ordinary interval suggests is imprecision in the sense 14.2.2 gives it. An earlier version of this field was a single string shared across every pooled estimand, and it asserted a disagreement between the two interval methods that is false of the estimand favouring neither arm -- where this object's own sensitivity verdict already said they agree. It is now written from the same two comparisons that verdict is written from. An earlier version still rested the downgrade on how MANY trials a pool contains; chapter 14 says in terms to avoid referring to the number of studies as a reason for imprecision, so that was both the wrong kind of reason and unsupported by the section cited. Section 10.10.4.5 is cited for the interval COMPARISON and not as a rule that the conservative interval decides the question.
imprecision.ois_note: The optimal information size is a condition section 14.2.2 makes part of adequate precision, and it is NOT computable from what this object holds: it needs an assumed control-arm risk and a target difference that no field here carries. It is UNKNOWN rather than satisfied, and this sentence exists so its absence cannot read as a pass.

Funnel-plot and regression methods for small-study effects are not interpretable at this size, so no assessment is made and none is implied. What can be said without a test is recorded instead and is not offered as a substitute for one: every contributing trial on this estimand is REGISTERED and published a primary report, and the trials in this field that did not meet their primary endpoints published that result plainly, which this object can state because most of the trials it holds are in that position. The word prospectively is deliberately absent from this sentence even though it is true of most of these trials, because it is NOT establishable from the record of one of them and a domain that quantifies over an estimand's trials must be true of each. Where it IS establishable the risk-of-bias domain says so. Rated not assessable, which downgrades nothing on its own.

It is a rating of an average across two different iron preparations, two different comparators and two different masking arrangements, on the recurrent composite. This object holds six estimands with six separate ratings and they are not interchangeable: a reader who takes the rating from one and the number from another has produced a claim this object does not make.

house_rule_interval_2026_08_18.THE_POINT_ESTIMATE_IS_UNCHANGED: The published point is 0.8066 and the house-rule point is 0.8066. THE NUMBER A READER REMEMBERS DOES NOT MOVE; what differs is the precision claim. That is why nothing downstream catches this -- every memorable quantity survives.

The trial enrolled 304 and randomised 152 to each arm; three patients were excluded from that set for having no post-baseline efficacy assessment, leaving the pair printed in the paper's own baseline and outcome tables and in the United States label. Both figures are real and they are not interchangeable. The stored cell they appeared in remains unsupported, and the reason is now precise rather than general: its treatment-arm numerator is the count of PLACEBO patients hospitalised for worsening heart failure, its control-arm numerator matches no row in the paper, and its effect estimate matches no analysis in the paper. Three of the four numbers have real provenance and none belongs to the row it sat on.

claims_corrected.claim: that FAIR-HF2's second primary endpoint may be pooled with the recurrent composite primaries of the other two large trials
claims_corrected.correction: It may not, and this is the correction with the largest effect on what this object computes. That endpoint counts heart-failure hospitalisations and carries NO cardiovascular-death component -- the publication names it as total heart failure hospitalizations and the registry describes it as a rate of total first and recurrent events of hospitalisations for heart failure. The two trials it was to be pooled with both include cardiovascular death in their primary. Pooling the three would combine a composite with a non-composite because all three are rate ratios below one, which is the exact conflation this object is built to refuse. The estimate is held in a separate recurrent hospitalisation-only estimand whose like-for-like partner is the other trial's total hospitalisation rate ratio.

claims_corrected.claim: that the trials missed by the living search were missed because of a completed-only status filter, a hardcoded drug whitelist or a wrong population ontology
claims_corrected.correction: None of those three explains the miss that matters most. The MOST RECENT trial in this review -- which is NOT its largest, and an earlier version of this correction called it both -- names its interventions in the registry only as iron and as saline; no brand name and no international non-proprietary name appears in that field at all. The trial is completed, phase 4 and randomised in a heart-failure population, so it passes a status filter, a phase filter and an allocation filter, and remains invisible to any query keyed on a drug name however complete the list of names. The correction is to key the search on the intervention CLASS, and the rediscovery test that demonstrates it is staged with both queries and both results.

claims_corrected.claim: that a heart-failure indication for intravenous iron implies a regulator assessment of heart-failure EVENTS
claims_corrected.correction: The United States label does carry a heart-failure indication and it is narrower than the phrase suggests: it authorises treatment of iron deficiency in adults with New York Heart Association class II or III heart failure TO IMPROVE EXERCISE CAPACITY. Its clinical-studies section for that indication rests on one trial and on the six-minute walk distance, and a scan of the whole document for hazard, rate ratio, odds ratio, risk ratio, win ratio and relative risk returns nothing. So the regulator layer is FOUND for one cell in this object and holds no event estimate for any other -- which is why it is recorded found on one row and not available, with that as the reason, on the rest. The label for the other molecule does not contain the phrase heart failure at all.

SCOPE:four-measures-never-merged.decision: This review reports SIX outcomes under FOUR effect measures and pools within three of them and across none. A rate over recurrent events, a hazard of a first event, a win ratio over pairs and a mean difference in metres are four different quantities. TWO of the four print ratios below one that a reader will read the same way; the win ratio prints a ratio ABOVE one whose direction is inverted relative to them, and the mean difference prints metres against a null of zero. An earlier version of this decision said three of the four print below one, miscounting in the direction that makes the object look more uniform than it is.
SCOPE:four-measures-never-merged.conformance: Section 10.3 gives the method every pool here uses, which is generic inverse variance on the log scale. The refusal to combine across the estimands is licensed by their falling under different sections rather than by a rule invented here: recurrent counts and rates are governed by 10.8, time-to-first analyses by 10.9, and the continuous outcome by 6.5.1.1 for its measure and 10.5.2 for its being a change score. THE WIN RATIO IS THE ONE MEASURE HERE THAT NO HANDBOOK SECTION GOVERNS, and this object says so rather than borrowing one. The strings win ratio and hierarchical composite appear NOWHERE in chapter 6 or chapter 10 -- checked by fetching both chapters, not assumed. An earlier version of this decision held the win ratio apart under 10.9, which is the TIME-TO-EVENT section: it concerns log hazard ratios and observed-minus-expected forms, and a pairwise hierarchical comparison is neither. Citing it was the defect this object names elsewhere -- a section governing the MEASURE a decision is about rather than the decision itself. What the refusal actually rests on is the estimand's own form, stated without borrowed authority: the quantity counts PAIRS rather than participants or events, its direction of benefit is inverted relative to every other ratio here, and its interval is not at the level the others use. Entering it into a hazard-ratio pool would not merely mislabel it, it would reverse the sign of the trial's finding. Section 3.2.4 is cited instead, because defining and grouping a review's outcomes is exactly what it governs, and the absence of a section for this measure is recorded as an absence.

SCOPE:direction-is-per-outcome-not-globa.decision: Each outcome declares its OWN direction of benefit. Two of the six outcomes here are beneficial upward and four are beneficial downward, so a single global rule reading below one as benefit would be wrong about a third of this object.
SCOPE:direction-is-per-outcome-not-globa.conformance: Section 3.2.4 governs how a review selects and describes its outcomes, and the direction an outcome improves in is part of describing it. The page this object replaces is the reason the decision is recorded rather than assumed: a template that renders a ratio below one as benefit across a whole object would render this review's hierarchical primary backwards, and would render the walk-distance endpoint -- whose null is zero, not one -- as something that has no meaning at all.

SCOPE:interval-level-is-read-not-assumed.decision: Every stored interval carries its own LEVEL and the standard error is derived using the multiplier belonging to that level. One cell in this object is not at the level the rest use, because its trial set a different significance level for that endpoint.
SCOPE:interval-level-is-read-not-assumed.conformance: Section 10.3 makes the standard error the input to an inverse-variance synthesis, and a standard error read off an interval is only as good as the multiplier used to read it. Reading the odd interval here at the ordinary level would return a standard error roughly a third too large and would UNDER-weight the largest trial in this review -- an error in the conservative direction, which is exactly the kind that survives review because nothing looks too good.

SCOPE:comparator-admits-usual-care.decision: ELIGIBILITY admits a comparator of placebo OR usual care. That is not generosity: one contributing trial randomised against usual care, and a placebo-only criterion would have excluded it. That is a property of a QUERY and the staged search record documents it as one, noting that the corrected query deliberately carries no comparator requirement. It is NOT one of the ways the replaced artefact lost trials -- that artefact's allow-list contains this very trial -- and an earlier version of this decision said it was.
SCOPE:comparator-admits-usual-care.conformance: Section 3.2.3 makes the comparator an eligibility axis, and this review sets that axis wide and then DECLARES the consequence rather than hiding it: on the one pooled estimand where the two comparator types meet, the uniformity table records the axis as differing and the risk-of-bias domain carries the open-label design of the usual-care trial. Section 10.10.1 is why that belongs in the uniformity table: it is clinical and methodological diversity, which no heterogeneity statistic computed from two numbers can see.

SCOPE:significance-travels-with-the-numb.decision: Trial-level significance is stored as a FIELD on every measured cell, with the p value, the multiplicity rule that governs it and whether the trial itself declares the result significant. Where this object cannot tell, the field records that it cannot rather than guessing.
SCOPE:significance-travels-with-the-numb.conformance: This review holds a cell whose interval excludes the null on a trial that is NEGATIVE by its own prespecified multiplicity rule, and the two facts are not in conflict -- they answer different questions. Prose saying so would be a paragraph a reader can leave behind; a field travels with the number into every view that renders the cell. Section 3.2.4 governs how a review describes the outcomes it reports, and 14.2.2 is why the distinction matters to certainty: an interval is one of the inputs to the imprecision domain and a multiplicity rule is not, so conflating them would corrupt a GRADE domain as well as a sentence.

SCOPE:pooled-significance-is-not-trial-s.decision: On the recurrent-composite estimand BOTH contributing trials report a p value above the conventional threshold on this endpoint and an interval that includes the null, while the POOLED ordinary interval excludes it. This object reports both, states that they are not in conflict, and does not headline the pooled result as though the trials had found what they did not. The wording is deliberately about what the papers PRINT: neither abstract uses the phrase not significant about its own primary endpoint, and an earlier version of this decision said they did, which is a claim about the sources that the sources do not carry.
SCOPE:pooled-significance-is-not-trial-s.conformance: Pooling two estimates increases precision, so a pooled interval excluding a null that both contributing intervals include is ordinary arithmetic under section 10.10.4 rather than a paradox. What section 10.10.4.5 adds, and what this object carries into the imprecision domain under 14.2.2, is that at two studies the more conservative interval method may be preferable, and on this estimand that interval INCLUDES the null. So the object reports the pooled figure, reports both trials' own findings on the cells, reports the conservative interval beside the ordinary one, and downgrades certainty for imprecision. The one thing it does not do is choose one of those and present it alone.

SCOPE:regulator-holds-one-cell.decision: The regulator layer is recorded as holding exactly ONE cell in this object, and as holding nothing on the other nine for two different reasons depending on which molecule the trial used. There is no global sentence in this object about what the regulator holds.
SCOPE:regulator-holds-one-cell.conformance: A United States heart-failure indication for one of these products does exist and it is narrower than its name: it authorises treatment to improve exercise capacity, and the clinical-studies section supporting it rests on one trial and one functional endpoint. The label for the other molecule does not contain the phrase heart failure at all. Writing one sentence about the regulator would have been false of one of the two products on either reading, which is the defect class this batch has spent the most rounds on.

The point estimates agree to two decimal places across a threefold difference in evidence, and their interval is WIDER than ours despite three times the patients -- which is what a Bayesian random-effects model with between-trial variance does, and is worth a reader's attention because the naive expectation is the opposite.

divergence_decomposed.ours: Rate ratio 0.8066 (0.6856 to 0.9488) for recurrent heart-failure hospitalisations together with cardiovascular death, k=2, AFFIRM-AHF and IRONMAN, from published summary data.
divergence_decomposed.theirs: RR 0.81 (0.69 to 0.95) on the same two trials (Clin Res Cardiol 2023); RR 0.81 (0.63 to 0.97) on six trials with individual participant data (Nat Med 2025); RR 0.73 (0.48 to 0.99) on four trials with harmonised definitions (Eur J Heart Fail 2023).
divergence_decomposed.why_they_differ: On the same two trials they do not differ at all. Across the wider analyses the difference is ACCESS, not method: individual participant data let those authors derive a recurrent-events composite for four trials that publish none, and no amount of care with published summaries can substitute for that. The honest statement is that our k=2 is the limit of what the published layer supports, and that where the layers overlap the numbers agree.

remainder_dispositions.what_this_says: SIXTEEN OF THE TWENTY-NINE ARE ELIGIBLE. Only 13 fail a stated criterion. The evidence base is not limited by eligibility -- it is limited by ESTIMAND MATCH and by trials that have not reported. Reporting all 29 as 'excluded' would have said the opposite, and would have been the withholding class again: eligible evidence recorded as though it had failed a test.
remainder_dispositions.largest_pending: ICONIC-HF (NCT06929806, n=1900, RECRUITING) registers cardiovascular death and hospitalisation for worsening heart failure -- THE SAME ESTIMAND AS THIS OBJECT'S HEADLINE POOL -- and will be the single largest contributor when it reports. INFERRCT (NCT05759078, n=1000) is the second.
remainder_dispositions.notable_eligible_not_poolable: FAIR-HF (NCT00520780, n=456) is the trial that established ferric carboxymaltose in heart failure. It meets P/I/C and its primary -- patient global assessment plus NYHA class -- is a registered functional primary a regulator relied on, so it PASSES the outcome criterion. It is not poolable because that is an ordinal patient-reported scale matching none of this object's six estimands. ELIGIBLE AND NOT POOLED is the correct reading; recording a landmark trial as 'excluded' would misstate why it is absent.

restated_2026_08_19_trailing_placebo.why_the_remainder_does_not_move: BOTH MOVERS WENT INTO NOT_ASSESSABLE, WHICH IS NOT A SCREENING QUEUE. k3 is unchanged at 34, so the 29-trial remainder and its dispositions stand exactly as screened. TERMINATED at n=6. Exercise capacity; no shared estimand.

iCHF-2. Primaries are LVEF and atrial-fibrillation burden -- surrogates. n=8, TERMINATED.
IronEx, WITHDRAWN, enrolment 0.

FAIR-HF, n=456, COMPLETED -- the trial that established FCM in heart failure. FCM vs normal saline; meets P/I/C, and its primary (patient global assessment plus NYHA class) is a registered functional primary a regulator relied on, so it PASSES the outcome criterion. It is not poolable: PGA/NYHA is an ordinal patient-reported scale, matching none of this object's six estimands. Iron sucrose -- fails the FCM/FDI criterion.

Mitochondrial function -- mechanistic. n=20, TERMINATED.
COREVIVE-HFpEF, n=170, status UNKNOWN. FDI vs placebo, 6-minute-walk primary; same position as COREVIVE-HFrEF.
Roxadustat, a HIF prolyl-hydroxylase inhibitor. Not intravenous iron at all.

ICONIC-HF, n=1900, RECRUITING. Ferric derisomaltose versus NO intravenous iron -- the 'usual care' half of the comparator criterion admits it. Primary is cardiovascular deaths and hospitalisations for worsening heart failure: THE SAME ESTIMAND AS THIS OBJECT'S HEADLINE POOL. It will be the single largest contributor when it reports.
ERADAL-HF uses iron sucrose IV and ferric polymaltose INTRAMUSCULARLY -- fails both the FCM/FDI criterion and, for one arm, the intravenous-route criterion.
iCHF. Primary is change in left-ventricular ejection fraction -- a surrogate. n=18, TERMINATED.

risk_of_bias.handbook: Higgins JPT, Savovic J, Page MJ, Elbers RG, Sterne JAC. Chapter 8: Assessing risk of bias in a randomized trial. In: Cochrane Handbook for Systematic Reviews of Interventions version 6.5.1
risk_of_bias.unit_of_assessment: A RESULT, not a study -- Handbook 8.2: 'risk of bias is assessed for a specific result'. Every judgement below names its outcome.
risk_of_bias.default_rule: A domain that cannot be judged from the registration and the published report is NO_INFORMATION, never LOW. Low-by-default asserts a fact; high-by-default invents a defect.

ceiling.statement: NO RESULT IN THIS REVIEW CAN REACH LOW RISK OF BIAS ON THE EVIDENCE WE CAN REACH, AND THAT IS A FACT ABOUT OUR ACCESS RATHER THAN ABOUT THE TRIALS. The two domains that would distinguish LOW from SOME CONCERNS need documents this review does not hold: D1 needs allocation concealment and baseline data, which are in neither the registration nor the published abstract; D5 needs the trial's statistical analysis plan, which is not held for any trial. SOME CONCERNS IS THEREFORE THE CEILING, NOT A FINDING. A trial rated SOME CONCERNS here may well be at low risk of bias -- we cannot show it, and we do not imply the opposite.
ceiling.what_would_change_it: Retrieving each trial's full published report and its statistical analysis plan or protocol. Until then the rating is bounded by what we read, and the bound is reported rather than the reader inferring it.
ceiling.why_this_is_stated_rather_than_left_impl: A rating of SOME CONCERNS with no explanation reads as a judgement against the trial. Omitting the reason would manufacture a criticism exactly as a low-by-default manufactures a reassurance -- the same defect pointed the other way.

manuscript.introduction:
This review asks: In adults with heart failure and iron deficiency, what is the effect of intravenous iron compared with placebo or usual care on recurrent hospitalisations for heart failure with and without cardiovascular death, on the time to a first such event, on death from any cause, on a hierarchical composite of death, hospitalisation and walk distance, and on exercise capacity itself -- with each of those questions answered separately?

It pools 2 randomised trials, against a saline placebo, except on the recurrent-composite estimand where one contributing trial randomised against usual care.

The outcomes pooled are Recurrent hospitalisations for heart failure together with cardiovascular death, as a rate ratio; Time to a FIRST cardiovascular death or hospitalisation for heart failure, as a hazard ratio; Recurrent hospitalisations for heart failure ALONE, with no death component, as a rate ratio; Time to death from ANY cause, as a hazard ratio; A hierarchical composite of death, hospitalisations for heart failure and change in walk distance, as an unmatched win ratio; Change in six-minute walk distance at the primary timepoint, in metres.

bookkeeping_2026_08_21.which_risk_of_bias_domains_drove_the_rat: Where a result is rated worse than LOW overall, the domain carrying that judgement is: D3 on 7 result(s), D1 on 3 result(s), D2 on 3 result(s), D5 on 3 result(s), D4 on 1 result(s).
